Prusa Polymers a. s. represents one of the key companies of the Prusa Research group, a highly innovative and fast-growing 3D printing company founded by Mr. Josef Průša in 2012. Within a few years, it has become the leading manufacturer of FFF/FDM 3D printers, with roughly a 10% share of the global desktop 3D printer market. The product range was further expanded with the introduction of an SLA 3D printer and with in-house research, development, and production of filament (thermoplastic feedstock, a thin plastic strand) for 3D printing.
The outstanding quality of Prusa Research’s 3D printers was confirmed many times by recognized companies and media, such as 3D Printing Industry Awards (Personal Printer of the Year – 2019, 2018) or Make: Magazine (Best Overall, Outstanding Open Software, Best Value…).
Due to their leading-edge performance, the Original Prusa 3D printers are used by professionals in various industries, such as automotive, entertainment, medical, etc. Aerospace customers of Prusa 3D printers and filaments are represented by key players including European Space Agency (ESA), NASA, and SpaceX, as well as airplane production companies such as Aero Vodochody Aerospace, Blanik Aircraft CZ, Latitude Aerospace Solutions, and Magellan Aerospace.
Prusa Polymers a. s. has its own scientific research capacities, including laboratories enabling in-house material development, a significant part of which is focused on the development of new polymer blends adapted for ideal processing on FDM 3D printers. Using advanced equipment for laboratory development and industrial production of filaments for 3D printing, the company also focuses on testing of thermo-mechanical characteristics of such materials, and their printing properties. The quality of the R&D capacities is also backed by several projects supported by the Technology Agency of the Czech Republic (TACR).

BONN Elektronik was founded in 1975 for production and sales of RF components and systems. Very soon development and production of a wide range of different power amplifiers and RF-systems became the main activity.
BONN amplifiers have made their good name with high quality and reliability in worldwide stationary and mobile applications. Resulting from the increasing demand, the company had to build a larger building in 2010. 
For more than 40 years our aim has been to advise our customers comprehensively in planning and realizing RF- and microwave systems. We are performant and flexible in developing innovative solutions for our customers. Starting from the quotation phase via delivery and installation of the instruments including maintenance we offer a complete service all from one source. Our development and production teams work on the basis of ISO 9001 total quality management. For many years all our instruments already have complied with CE-standards and VDE safety regulations.
A complete range of measurement instruments, workstations and machines is supporting our engineers to solve most of the jobs inhouse.
EDA software for simulation and calculation of linear and non-linear RF-circuits
EDA based PCB design by means of up-to-date interactive topological auto-routers considering actual EMI practice
CAD-CAM connection from design software to most modern precision CNC milling machines and lathes
Spectrum and network analyzers up to 40 GHz
Photoplotter, recycling etching machine, tinning facility, climatic test chamber and special tools
Measurement setups for individual testing of all instruments for conducted emissions and instrument safety according to VDE regulations
Highly committed employees with long experience in RF technology solve complex demands as required by our customers. We are your competent partner and offer “the power you need”.
The success of BONN Elektronik in high power RF amplifiers led to the founding of a subsidiary in Budapest in 1991. BONN Hungary Electronics focuses on development and production of components and subsystems for mobile communication as well as customized RF synthesizers and oscillators (see product overview).

entityDescription: The PBL Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency is the Dutch national institute for strategic policy analysis in the field of environment, nature and spatial planning. PBL is a part of the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management, though fully independent as far as the contents of its work is concerned. PBL is particularly experienced in integrated assessments of key environmental issues that go beyond a sectoral approach, analysing the causes and effects of environmental change. It evaluates and assesses policies at regional, national, European and global scale. PBL bases its studies on extensive data analyses, modelling and scenario analyses, maintaining an active dialogue with both the scientific community and policymakers. PBL is strong in biophysical disciplines, but also has expertise in the fields of economy and governance. Over the past decades, it has cooperated with international organizations such as the OECD, UNEP and IPCC as well as operated in European networks. PBL has leading roles in projects for DG Environment, DG Climate Action and DG Research & Innovation, contributing to climate policies and supporting EU policy development. PBL is also the eldest Collaborating Centre to UNEP for Reporting Assessment and Forecasting. Senior staff members serve on panels such as UNEP’s International Resource Panel, co-leading the work on Food and on Cities.

Kersnikova Institute is a non-profit cultural institution operating in the fields of investigative arts, culture, and educational practices, with an emphasis on a future society that is intertwined with modern technologies and science. As an active production platform, Kersnikova enables valuable interdisciplinary interactions between creative individuals, institutions and companies, produces and showcases inspiring works of art, enables intensive public debate, facilitates investigative learning workshops for all ages, and encourages creative individuals to collaborate with the economy in developing social and product innovations. 
Kersnikova Institute combines the contemporary investigative art activities of Kapelica Gallery with activities of Rampa mechatronics laboratory, the BioTehna biotechnology laboratory, which focuses on the artistic research of living systems, and the Vivarium, where animals, plants, and robots meet.
Kapelica Gallery is one of the leading venues for contemporary investigative art on a global scale. Its program, which consists of spatial installations, performances, sound research, and theoretical and critical lectures, focuses on scientific and technological applications, biopolitics, and urban phenomena, which addresses both professional and general public. The gallery’s program is focused on responding to profound changes in a society saturated with new technologies. The program is therefore built from artistic activities that reflect various social phenomena of the present and predict possible future scenarios.
The BioTehna laboratory is a place where complex art projects involving various biological systems are developed, experiments are carried out, and interesting connections between biological materials and technology are explored. At BioTehna, artists and scientists creatively and innovatively combine living systems with electronic technologies into hybrid or symbiotic coexistence, thus exploring the possibilities of their coexistence and coevolution.
Rampa is a laboratory for mechatronics where electronics is programmed, developed and various devices are assembled. The experimental environment is intended for individuals and groups, interested in creative research into new as well as outdated technologies. In conjunction with the other two laboratories, various approaches in the field of mechatronics are tested through possible connections to living systems. The activities of artists, scientists, and engineers of all three laboratories critically thematize the phenomenology of artificial life and thus create the conditions for a better understanding of life and its emancipated interdependence with modern technologies.
More than 25 years of daily activities have created hundreds of unforgettable moments and experiences that have given shape and meaning to contemporaneity as we currently understand it. Today, we transfer these experiences through non-formal investigative learning to children, youth, and the interested public by systematically implementing a capacity development program through interactive workshops led by mentors which are educated through our mentoring program.
The acquired knowledge, inspired by visions of all the possible futures is the starting point for establishing programs for the involvement of creative people in the processes of social and product innovation. By participating in innovation processes with the help of innovation catalysts, we introduce art-thinking and design-thinking for both communities and companies, for more radical, sustainable, and ethical solutions that create opportunities for a better future for individuals and society.

Company description: Kersnikova Institute is a non-profit cultural institution operating in the fields of investigative arts, culture, and educational practices, with an emphasis on a future society that is intertwined with modern technologies and science. As an active production platform, Kersnikova enables valuable interdisciplinary interactions between creative individuals, institutions and companies, produces and showcases inspiring works of art, enables intensive public debate, facilitates investigative learning workshops for all ages, and encourages creative individuals to collaborate with the economy in developing social and product innovations. 
Kersnikova Institute combines the contemporary investigative art activities of Kapelica Gallery with activities of Rampa mechatronics laboratory, the BioTehna biotechnology laboratory, which focuses on the artistic research of living systems, and the Vivarium, where animals, plants, and robots meet.
Kapelica Gallery is one of the leading venues for contemporary investigative art on a global scale. Its program, which consists of spatial installations, performances, sound research, and theoretical and critical lectures, focuses on scientific and technological applications, biopolitics, and urban phenomena, which addresses both professional and general public. The gallery’s program is focused on responding to profound changes in a society saturated with new technologies. The program is therefore built from artistic activities that reflect various social phenomena of the present and predict possible future scenarios.
The BioTehna laboratory is a place where complex art projects involving various biological systems are developed, experiments are carried out, and interesting connections between biological materials and technology are explored. At BioTehna, artists and scientists creatively and innovatively combine living systems with electronic technologies into hybrid or symbiotic coexistence, thus exploring the possibilities of their coexistence and coevolution.
Rampa is a laboratory for mechatronics where electronics is programmed, developed and various devices are assembled. The experimental environment is intended for individuals and groups, interested in creative research into new as well as outdated technologies. In conjunction with the other two laboratories, various approaches in the field of mechatronics are tested through possible connections to living systems. The activities of artists, scientists, and engineers of all three laboratories critically thematize the phenomenology of artificial life and thus create the conditions for a better understanding of life and its emancipated interdependence with modern technologies.
More than 25 years of daily activities have created hundreds of unforgettable moments and experiences that have given shape and meaning to contemporaneity as we currently understand it. Today, we transfer these experiences through non-formal investigative learning to children, youth, and the interested public by systematically implementing a capacity development program through interactive workshops led by mentors which are educated through our mentoring program.
The acquired knowledge, inspired by visions of all the possible futures is the starting point for establishing programs for the involvement of creative people in the processes of social and product innovation. By participating in innovation processes with the help of innovation catalysts, we introduce art-thinking and design-thinking for both communities and companies, for more radical, sustainable, and ethical solutions that create opportunities for a better future for individuals and society.

Digiotouch (DIGI) is a fast-growing SME providing secure, sustainable Digital Transformation products and services. DIGI operates in four industry verticals - Digital Healthcare, Agri-Food, Industry 4.0, and Smart Cities. DIGI’s core competence is to digitize customers' legacy business processes, operations, and assets using two core products - Cloud based, secure Paradise IoT Platform and Digiotouch Edge. The company provides open standard based digital solutions powering next-gen devices and services for the EU Digital Single Market initiative. The Paradise IoT Platform includes several common service functions (e.g. remote monitoring, device management, visualization, end-to-end security, secure storage, privacy), and “Academy for IoT” - a Digital Learning Hub to educate the next-gen workforce on Digital Transformation. The Platform has been utilized by six organizations from the USA, UK, India, and Malaysia. On the technical front, DIGI is pioneering “Digital-First'' strategies which are broadly based on Blockchain, Cybersecurity, Intelligent Cloud & Edge Computing, ICT Standards (e.g. W3C Web of Things, IEEE P2145 - Standard for Framework and Definitions for Blockchain Governance), Machine Learning, and Mobile Apps. 
DIGI has been one of the winners of the EU Datathon 2018 competition. The ground-breaking industrial research & innovation activities of the company has received funding from several EU H2020 projects – upPE-T, BlockStart, DIH-HERO, DIGI-B-CUBE, Block.IS, Logistics for Manufacturing SMEs (L4MS), Fed4FIRE+, StandICT.eu, and Triangle. The company has also been accepted in the EIT Health Living Labs and Test Beds Programme to validate its business model and scale-up strategies for its digital therapeutics’ mobile app AMICA. DIGI is also experienced in managing consortia of cascade funding (e.g. FSTP) projects and has successfully completed and delivered several such projects. In addition to industrial R&D, DIGI has strong experience in market research, business development, product commercialization, and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). The company has successfully integrated all the previous EU-funded project outcomes into its core products enhancing their commercial portfolio.

We are a manufacturer of special bolts and have developed the ability to connect our products (via a fiber optic sensor) to qualify a tightening and control the integrity of the assembly. 
The principle is to integrate a fiber optic sensor housed in its center to screws, studs, and other threaded rods. 
The fiber optic technology used is a patented process based on optical interferometry and allows to calculate the minute variations in lengths by emission of a light (spectrum of a light wave). It is projected onto a set of mirrors and its feedback signals are analysed to determine the lengthening of the bolt to 0.5 µm/m of precision. 
The C-Bolt® can be installed at all industrial sites and in all areas of intervention. It is not only insensitive to rays (nuclear zone), magnetic fields, distances (maximum 3.5 km from its base), temperatures (from -268 to 320 degrees Celsius), ATEX zones, pressure (maxi 300 bars), wetlands (subaquatic), and frequencies. Moreover, by its passive constitution, it does not emit any disturbance.

Focusing on the industry and education segments, Giant Lazer provides innovative VR and AR applications: immersive training programs for employees and students, advanced simulators, as well as process and data visualizations and assisted reality applications for smart glasses.

We are helping workers boost efficiency with specialized software solutions.

Working within multiple industries — logistics, automation and robotics, automotive, educational, and many others., we help clients navigate through a rapidly evolving landscape of new technologies. Pilz Poland,

ING,
Dutch and Swiss branches of KPMG.
